# Device Overview {#sec-overview}

This reference documents a compact controller and its register-level interface. The architecture follows the conventions described by @arm2020cortexm.

::: {.audio-chunk #s1.1p1}
This section introduces the embedded controller engineering reference and its register-level interface.
:::

## Pin Definitions {#sec-pins}

| Pin | Name | Direction | Description |
|:---:|:-----|:---------:|:------------|
| 1 | VDD | Power | 3.3 volt supply |
| 2 | GND | Power | Ground return |
| 3 | PA0 | I/O | General-purpose input/output |
| 4 | UART_TX | Output | Serial transmit line |

Table: Controller pin definitions. {#tbl-pinout}

::: {.callout-note}
The GPIO bank is reset to a safe input state after power-on.
:::

## Register Map {#sec-registers}

The generated map in @tbl-registers complements the pin assignment in @tbl-pinout.

```{python}
#| label: tbl-registers
#| tbl-cap: "Controller register map"
from IPython.display import Markdown, display
from tabulate import tabulate

registers = [["CTRL", "0x00", "Enable and mode"], ["STATUS", "0x04", "Ready flags"]]
display(Markdown(tabulate(registers, headers=["Register", "Offset", "Purpose"], tablefmt="pipe")))
```

::: {.callout-warning}
Writes to reserved register bits must use zero values to preserve forward compatibility.
:::

## Timing Characteristic {#sec-timing}

The representative response curve is shown in @fig-response.

```{python}
#| label: fig-response
#| fig-cap: "Representative controller response"
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

sample_times = [0, 1, 2, 3, 4]
sample_response = [0.0, 0.35, 0.62, 0.82, 0.93]
plt.plot(sample_times, sample_response, marker="o")
plt.xlabel("Time (ms)")
plt.ylabel("Normalized response")
plt.grid(True, alpha=0.3)
plt.tight_layout()
```

The timing profile is illustrative and should be replaced with measured data before release.
